A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FNOPE and retain the same core method and four application areas. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.5 and the appendices report original inference experiments on linear Gaussian, SIRD, Darcy flow, and Antarctic ice-shelf problems, including quantitative metrics and posterior visualizations.

after.justification: The original empirical studies remain, supplemented by hyperparameter ablations, lower-budget experiments, computational measurements, and an iFNO comparison.

M1.justification: The FNO architecture, flow-matching objective, Gaussian-process base distribution, lengthscale heuristic, masking and positional augmentation, FFT variant, and vector-parameter head remain unchanged. The newly evaluated no-jitter variant is an ablation rather than a replacement of the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The four application areas remain. The new Gaussian stress test changes the prior lengthscale from 0.05 to 0.005, introducing higher-frequency functions as a distinct test condition (S5.1, S7.1). The 20-point SIRD and 500-parameter ice experiments already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix S8.2 and Figure S9 newly compare Long et al.'s invertible Fourier Neural Operator with FNOPE and FNOPE (fix) on Darcy flow. The original NPE, FMPE, and Simformer comparator memberships remain in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: S2.2 revises the stated calibration aggregation from pooled ranks to averaging per-marginal EoDs. V2 adds 100-simulation settings for Gaussian and ice experiments, controlled hyperparameter sweeps, and an iFNO training protocol. Gaussian spectral padding changes from 200 to 20, while S4.1 now discards the zero imaginary Fourier coefficient. These are reported protocol changes; reruns of retained results are not established.

E4.justification: New analyses test Fourier-mode sufficiency and spectral recovery, masking density, base-distribution lengthscale, and positional jitter across Gaussian, SIRD, and Darcy tasks (S7.1–S7.3). Figure S9 adds error and posterior-variance diagnostics for iFNO. These substantially expand design validation beyond the retained sparse-observation and higher-dimensional ice studies.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds/runs and mean ± standard error for performance reporting. Posterior standard-deviation visualizations also predate v2. No increased run count, new confidence-interval practice, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 6 add results at 100 training simulations. New ablations report frequency-recovery and hyperparameter-sensitivity findings. Figure S9 reports comparable predictive MSE for iFNO but calibration error around 0.25 and nearly vanishing posterior variance. Tables S1–S3 add extensive timing measurements; these are new results rather than demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: S2.2 changes the mathematical definition of calibration aggregation, although its final averaging equation omits a summation symbol. S8.2 adds a derivation of EoD = 0.25 for collapsed point estimates under equally likely overprediction and underprediction. The original kernel-lengthscale derivation remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: simulation-efficient function-valued posterior inference, flexible discretizations, joint inference of vector-valued parameters, and scalability. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of mode and lengthscale sensitivity and explains iFNO's uncertainty failure as posterior collapse. Section 4.2 attributes the Gaussian performance gap to positional noise broadening the likelihood, but S7.1 finds little difference when jitter is removed, leaving that explanation unreconciled. The original high-frequency, sparse-observation, and domain-dimensionality limitations remain.

D1.justification: Tables S1–S3 replace coarse runtime bounds and a Gaussian-only size table with task-wide model sizes, total/per-epoch training times, and sampling times. S8.2 supplies iFNO architecture and training settings. Reported Gaussian FMPE sizes change from 34,212/149,032 to 86.3K/299K without an explained architecture revision. Hardware and the code-access pointer remain.

R1.justification: Related work expands to marginal inference and additional neural operators, including sensitivity-constrained FNOs, GNOT, latent neural operators, Transolver, and iFNO. It more explicitly distinguishes joint Bayesian inference from deterministic inversion and other conditional models. Four implementation/simulator references are removed, while the main positioning relative to FUSE and function-space diffusion remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. Local explanations, notation, affiliations, and venue text are revised, and supplementary material is organized into ablations and additional results. The displayed joint loss disappears from Section 3.3 despite surviving surrounding references; the normalized loss remains in the appendix.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial multipanel ablation displays and the iFNO comparison, and expands the resource table into three task-grouped tables. Figures 3 and 6 extend their simulation-budget axes, and predictive-MSE labels are clarified. Existing Darcy sample, mean, and variance displays are retained as Figures S6–S8 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens design validation: the new ablations directly test frequency limitations and central hyperparameter choices, while the iFNO comparison distinguishes predictive accuracy from calibrated uncertainty. Detailed computational measurements also make practical efficiency assessable beyond v1's coarse bounds. These gains outweigh localized documentation defects, including the missing main-text loss, malformed calibration average, and unreconciled jitter explanation.
